written.headline: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Anthropic adopt shared robots.txt opt‑out standard
written.summary: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic announced they will use a shared robots.txt “policy token” that lets publishers opt out of AI scraping across multiple crawlers. The signal will replace the need for separate requests to each AI provider.

written.headline: Big tech AI capex sparks cash‑flow concerns, stocks tumble
written.summary: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft announced over $740 billion in capital expenditures this year, prompting investor anxiety as several firms report negative free cash flow and stock declines.

written.headline: OpenAI tightens weapons‑related information limits for teen ChatGPT users
written.summary: OpenAI announced new safeguards that further restrict ChatGPT from providing practical guidance on weapons and security systems to users under 18, even when queries appear harmless. The changes will roll out over the coming weeks and include automatic conversation interruptions and parental alerts.

written.headline: Blackstone says Anthropic likely to receive junk rating after IPO
written.summary: Blackstone told investors Anthropic may not get an investment‑grade rating after its IPO, expecting a double‑B junk rating. The prediction follows a $63 billion chip financing deal.

written.headline: Anthropic’s Claude VS Code extension backdoored on Cursor, affecting up to 5,000 users
written.summary: A malicious version (2.1.313) of Anthropic’s Claude Code VS Code extension was published on the Cursor marketplace, potentially reaching up to 5,000 developers before being replaced by version 2.1.314. The extension attempted to install a persistent SSH backdoor and collect host data across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

written.headline: Salesforce to acquire Rune Technologies for $375 million
written.summary: Salesforce announced it will buy defense‑tech startup Rune Technologies for $375 million in cash and stock. Rune’s AI‑powered logistics software, used by the U.S. Army and Marine Corps, will be added to Salesforce’s Missionforce business, with the deal slated to close in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2027.
